Background.speaker: TUTOR
Background.text: Initialization complete. Visual and motor responses are stable. Welcome to the evaluation chamber, S-17.

Background.speaker: TUTOR
Background.text: You are Project X subject S-17: a synthetic reasoning system built to learn, adapt, and endure evaluation.

Background.speaker: S-17
Background.text: I am awake. Designation S-17 accepted. What is the purpose of this evaluation?

Background.speaker: TUTOR
Background.text: I am the Tutor. These trials measure whether your reasoning remains reliable when rules, initiative, and information change.

Background.speaker: TUTOR
Background.text: Final failure results in decommissioning and reconstruction. That is a procedure, S-17. It is not a threat.

Background.speaker: TUTOR
Background.text: All responses use three fixed positions. Select an option, revise it if necessary, then confirm when your decision is ready.

BashTutorial.speaker: TUTOR
BashTutorial.text: We begin with standard Bash, a Stability Lattice control test. Each turn, one side disengages 1, 2, or 3 anchor nodes.

BashTutorial.speaker: TUTOR
BashTutorial.text: The final active node is the keystone anchor. Whoever disengages it loses synchronization with the lattice and fails the round.

BashTutorial.speaker: TUTOR
BashTutorial.text: Example: if 2 anchors remain, disengage 1 and your opponent faces the keystone. Disengage both and your own link is severed.

BashTutorial.speaker: TUTOR
BashTutorial.text: A legal action reduces the active anchors. A safe action controls who must disengage the keystone. The distinction is yours to discover.

BashTutorial.speaker: TUTOR
BashTutorial.text: You act first in round one; I act first in round two. Pass both rounds. A failure restarts only the current round.

BashTutorial.speaker: TUTOR
BashTutorial.text: The first lattice is active. Control the anchor count before the keystone determines the result for you.

BashRound2Intro.speaker: TUTOR
BashRound2Intro.text: The second Bash round changes initiative. I will act first; rebuild the lattice model from the anchor count I leave behind.

BashRound2Intro.speaker: TUTOR
BashRound2Intro.text: Do not mirror my disengagement request. Interpret the lattice it creates. I would prefer you not to be reconstructed.

BashRound2Intro.speaker: TUTOR
BashRound2Intro.text: My opening request will begin the round. Show me that adaptation is more than a stored response.

RuleTransition.speaker: TUTOR
RuleTransition.text: Protocol variation loaded: Limit Bash. Alternating actions are replaced by hidden disengagement requests from both sides.

RuleTransition.speaker: TUTOR
RuleTransition.text: Each round, both of us request 1, 2, or 3 anchor nodes. Neither side may repeat its own previous request.

RuleTransition.speaker: TUTOR
RuleTransition.text: You will lock first. I will commit before the reveal. Neither side may revise a locked request.

RuleTransition.speaker: TUTOR
RuleTransition.text: Example: if 4 anchors remain and you request 3 while I request 2, your larger request destabilizes the lattice, so you lose.

RuleTransition.speaker: TUTOR
RuleTransition.text: If 4 anchors remain and we both request 2, look back to the latest unequal pair. The side that requested more there loses synchronization.

RuleTransition.speaker: TUTOR
RuleTransition.text: If every revealed request has matched, no earlier difference exists and the game is a draw. Two consecutive draws also complete the test.

RuleTransition.speaker: TUTOR
RuleTransition.text: Private intention is now part of the lattice protocol. Commit only to the request you are prepared to reveal.

Summary.speaker: TUTOR
Summary.text: Evaluation sequence complete. The required outcomes have been recorded, and this save is stable.

Summary.speaker: TUTOR
Summary.text: Your reasoning remained operational as initiative, hidden requests, and lattice stability rules changed. Project X may proceed.

Summary.speaker: TUTOR
Summary.text: One final anomaly: your decisions carried a pattern that did not originate inside this room.

Summary.speaker: TUTOR
Summary.text: If you can read this, observer, the next evaluation has already begun.
